Import a character or robot, define how it moves, animate it on a timeline and send the same evaluated motion to a 3D preview, a 2D character, or real servos and controllers. The flagship of the Aether apps. An open alternative to Bottango.

> **Alpha 0.1 — early access.** Aether Animation is alpha software: features are incomplete,
> file formats may change between alphas, and it is not yet qualified for production
> work. Every feature below is marked as working today, in progress or planned.

## Features

### Works today

- ✅ **One animation engine** — Rigs with mates, joint limits and relations; kinematics (including DH chains); pose resolution, validation and evaluation in a renderer-independent engine.
- ✅ **The .anima format** — Characters and scenes saved in a versioned, documented format with validation and migration.
- ✅ **Headless show playback** — Scenes play without the editor: clips, poses, waits, event gates, variables and branches, loops and deterministic parallel tracks.
- ✅ **Hardware wire protocol** — A versioned wire protocol with a simulator and serial transport, so output can be proven before it reaches a servo.
- ✅ **Web workspace** — The animation workspace on the shared Aether interface: viewport, pose panel, mate and relation dialogs and a timeline.
- ✅ **Model Studio interface** — The shared Aether interface: a transparent document header, floating resizable side cards, a separate tool tray, saved layouts and themes — the same in every app.

### In progress

- 🔨 **Rig and joint authoring** — Typed joint editing, placement and handles directly in the viewport.
- 🔨 **Keyframe editing** — Editable keys and ranges, curves, interpolation and auto-key on the timeline.
- 🔨 **Hardware output** — Actuator mapping with inversion, neutral and limits, and explicit arm/disarm with failsafe.

### Planned

- 🗺️ **Servo and controller drivers** — Hobby servos and PCA9685 first, then steppers, DYNAMIXEL and custom channels.
- 🗺️ **Audio and video sync** — Waveforms, media tracks and lip-sync timing.
- 🗺️ **Puppeteering** — Record live input from controllers onto tracks, with layering and smoothing.
- 🗺️ **Advanced motion** — Pose blending, look-at, inverse kinematics and velocity-aware motion planning.

## Built-in AI · Planned

Connect ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini once in Aether Studio (**Plugins → My connections**).
Agents use the app's own commands — validated, undoable and recorded. AI is optional:
nothing you save ever needs it.

- The AI advisor comes to Animation through the same tool contract as every Aether app: inspect the rig, pose it and key it, with normal undo.
- AI is an authoring aid only: saved animation never requires an AI model to play, on screen or on hardware.
- The same tools are available from the command line and as MCP tools, with scoped permissions and safe retries.

Example: “Blink both eyes twice over one second, then turn the head 20° to the left.”

## On its own, or with Aether Studio

Aether Animation keeps its core features on a single machine. Connect it to
[Aether Studio](https://jenkinsrobotics.github.io/AetherStudio/), your own server, and it gains what a
team needs: access from any device, built-in AI, PDM with versions, branches and
releases, and multi-user sharing, comments and tasks. Characters, scenes and media live in Drive; shows deploy to players on the network; the team shares rigs and reviews performances together.

## What every Aether app brings

- **Runs on its own.** Open an app on one machine and work locally. Your files stay on your disk in open, documented formats. _(local install today · downloadable desktop app planned)_
- **Or on your own server.** Point the apps at an Aether Studio server — a Mac Studio in the office or a rack of machines — and the whole team works from one place.
- **Any device.** Every app is a web app first, so laptops, desktops and tablets connect through a browser — no install on the client. _(desktop downloads planned)_
- **Built-in AI.** Connect ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini once in Studio. Each app's AI advisor edits your open document with the app's own tools — and AI is never required to open or play your work.
- **PDM and version control.** Versions, branches, releases and obsolescence for every document, with a visual version graph and restore.
- **Multi-user.** One account across every app, shared workspaces, permissions, comments and tasks. _(real-time co-editing in progress)_
- **Command line and MCP.** Every agent tool is also a CLI command and an MCP tool, with scoped grants, revision guards and retry receipts.
- **Open source.** Apache-2.0. Own your tools, your files and your server.

## Roadmap

| Release | Focus | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha 0.1 | Engine and format | The animation engine, .anima files, headless playback and the wire protocol with its simulator. |
| Alpha 0.2 | Author on the timeline | Rig, joint and keyframe editing in the web workspace. |
| Beta | First servo | Actuator mapping and live output to a real servo, safely armed. |

## Get started

```sh
git clone --branch v0.1.0-alpha.1 --single-branch https://github.com/JenkinsRobotics/Aether-Animation.git
cd Aether-Animation
python3 tools/fetch-vendor.py
```

See [Alpha 0.1 setup and current limits](ALPHA_0_1.md) for frontend build and
server requirements. The web download is a frontend bundle, not a desktop installer.

See the [website](https://jenkinsrobotics.github.io/Aether-Animation/) for the full tour.

# aether-animation

Local migration candidate for Aether. Extracted from the current working source,
including uncommitted changes. **Production still uses the original Aether Studio
checkout.** Read `MIGRATION.md` before switching development to this folder.

## Build

Use Node 22.12+ and npm. From `web`:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
```

Shared Aether packages are versioned archives under `vendor/`, with lockfile
integrity checks. No frontend imports source from the original checkout. Archives
are temporary local distribution until the package registry is configured.
The platform serves these builds using `aether-platform/projects.json`.

The existing product README is retained as `README.pre-split.md` where present.
Some older paths in historical documentation refer to the former monorepo.
